answers.explanation: The verifier, not the token, decides which algorithms are acceptable.
The public key is public, so the attacker can sign tokens with it.
Some libraries once accepted it, letting anyone write their own claims.
With enough measurements an attacker could forge a signature byte by byte. Use hmac.compare_digest.
Clock skew is normal between machines.
HttpOnly cookies can't be read by scripts, but they open up CSRF instead.
SameSite stops the browser from sending the cookie on cross-site requests.
